title: Smartphone vs the classroom
titleChinese: 智能手机 vs 传统课堂
paragraphs: We know it’s good to learn another language. It opens doors, makes you more employable, helps you make new friends, and it’s fun too. But to improve our linguistic skills, many of us have to endure hours of school lessons or evening classes, with our heads buried in textbooks. It’s no wonder then that technology appears to be providing a better and more accessible way of learning.

There is certainly a huge demand for language learning, and having a smartphone means you can have a virtual teacher with you wherever you go. Many app developers are keen to cash in on the demand, and there are numerous learning apps available – including our own, free, BBC Learning English app! One of many popular apps, Duolingo, offers 91 courses in 30 languages and has more than 300 million users.

Some educational apps offer languages not popular enough to be taught at evening classes, or at most universities. And others offer ‘invented’ language courses in Esperanto, Elvish and Star Trek's Klingon – lessons you might not find in a traditional classroom. Whatever you want to learn, apps allow you to go at your own pace and fit learning around other commitments. But they’re not perfect – you might not get your head round the grammar and will lack the peer support you could get in a classroom environment.

So, does technology spell the end of traditional classrooms and teachers? Guy Baron, head of modern languages at Aberystwyth University, thinks not. He told the BBC that apps should be used alongside classroom methods, not to the exclusion of traditional teaching. And he adds: "The apps are very conversational... they're not designed for degrees, but they could be additional resources."

Certainly technology is going to help in and outside the classroom. But attending a real lesson, facing a real teacher, probably forces you to be more committed. Motivation can be a problem when using an app. But if you have a genuine and practical reason to learn another language, you will no doubt stick with it.

vocabulary.entry: linguistic skills /lɪŋˈɡwɪstɪk skɪlz/ 语言技能
vocabulary.example: Regular practice is key to improving your linguistic skills.
vocabulary.translation: 定期练习是提升语言技能的关键。

vocabulary.entry: accessible /əkˈsesəbl/ adj. 易获得的；便捷的
vocabulary.example: The online course is accessible to anyone with an internet connection.
vocabulary.translation: 只要有网络，任何人都能参加这门在线课程。

vocabulary.entry: virtual teacher /ˈvɜːtʃuəl ˈtiːtʃə(r)/ 虚拟老师
vocabulary.example: The language app uses a virtual teacher to guide users through lessons.
vocabulary.translation: 这款语言应用通过虚拟老师引导用户完成课程。

vocabulary.entry: cash in on /kæʃ ɪn ɒn/ 利用；从……中获利
vocabulary.example: Many companies are cashing in on the growing demand for eco-friendly products.
vocabulary.translation: 许多公司正利用人们对环保产品日益增长的需求获利。

vocabulary.entry: numerous /ˈnjuːmərəs/ adj. 众多的；许多的
vocabulary.example: She has made numerous friends through her language exchange group.
vocabulary.translation: 她通过语言交换小组结交了许多朋友。

vocabulary.entry: invented language /ɪnˈventɪd ˈlæŋɡwɪdʒ/ 人造语言
vocabulary.example: Esperanto is a well-known invented language designed for international communication.
vocabulary.translation: 世界语是一种为国际交流设计的著名人造语言。

vocabulary.entry: go at your own pace /ɡəʊ æt jɔː(r) əʊn peɪs/ 按照自己的节奏进行
vocabulary.example: The self-study course allows students to go at their own pace.
vocabulary.translation: 这门自学课程允许学生按照自己的节奏学习。

vocabulary.entry: fit around /fɪt əˈraʊnd/ 适应；迁就（安排时间）
vocabulary.example: I need to fit my language lessons around my work schedule.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要根据工作安排来调整语言课程的时间。

vocabulary.entry: get your head round /ɡet jɔː(r) hed raʊnd/ 理解；弄明白（复杂事物）
vocabulary.example: It took me a while to get my head round the complex grammar rules.
vocabulary.translation: 我花了好一会儿才弄明白这些复杂的语法规则。

vocabulary.entry: peer support /pɪə(r) səˈpɔːt/ 同伴支持；同侪互助
vocabulary.example: Peer support can make learning a new language less intimidating.
vocabulary.translation: 同伴支持能让学习新语言变得不那么令人胆怯。

vocabulary.entry: spell the end of /spel ði end ɒv/ 意味着……的终结
vocabulary.example: Some people think AI will spell the end of traditional jobs.
vocabulary.translation: 有些人认为人工智能将意味着传统工作的终结。

vocabulary.entry: alongside /əˌlɒŋˈsaɪd/ prep. 与……一起；除……之外
vocabulary.example: The new software will be used alongside existing systems.
vocabulary.translation: 这款新软件将与现有系统一起使用。

vocabulary.entry: to the exclusion of /tu ði ɪkˈskluːʒn ɒf/ 排除；不包括
vocabulary.example: He focuses on his work to the exclusion of all other interests.
vocabulary.translation: 他一心扑在工作上，排除了所有其他兴趣爱好。

vocabulary.entry: conversational /ˌkɒnvəˈseɪʃənl/ adj. 注重对话的；口语化的
vocabulary.example: The app provides conversational practice to help users speak more naturally.
vocabulary.translation: 这款应用提供口语对话练习，帮助用户更自然地表达。

vocabulary.entry: additional resources /əˈdɪʃənl rɪˈsɔːsɪz/ 额外资源
vocabulary.example: The teacher recommended some additional resources for further study.
vocabulary.translation: 老师推荐了一些额外资源供深入学习。

vocabulary.entry: committed /kəˈmɪtɪd/ adj. 投入的；尽心尽力的
vocabulary.example: She is a committed language learner who practices every day.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一位投入的语言学习者，每天都坚持练习。

vocabulary.entry: motivation /ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃn/ n. 动力；积极性
vocabulary.example: His main motivation for learning French is to travel to Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 他学习法语的主要动力是去巴黎旅行。

vocabulary.entry: genuine /ˈdʒenjuɪn/ adj. 真实的；真诚的
vocabulary.example: She has a genuine interest in learning about different cultures through language.
vocabulary.translation: 她对通过语言了解不同文化有着真诚的兴趣。

vocabulary.entry: practical /ˈpræktɪkl/ adj. 实际的；实用的
vocabulary.example: Learning basic phrases is more practical for travelers than mastering complex grammar.
vocabulary.translation: 对于旅行者来说，学习基本短语比掌握复杂语法更实用。

vocabulary.entry: stick with it /stɪk wɪð ɪt/ 坚持下去
vocabulary.example: Learning a language is challenging, but if you stick with it, you will succeed.
vocabulary.translation: 学习语言颇具挑战性，但只要坚持下去，你就会成功。

vocabulary.entry: endure /ɪnˈdjʊə(r)/ v. 忍受；承受
vocabulary.example: She endured many hours of practice to become fluent in Spanish.
vocabulary.translation: 为了能流利地说西班牙语，她忍受了数小时的练习。

vocabulary.entry: buried in /ˈberid ɪn/ 埋头于；专注于
vocabulary.example: He was buried in his language textbook and didn’t hear the doorbell.
vocabulary.translation: 他埋头于语言课本，没听见门铃响。

sentences.english: We know it’s good to learn another language.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道学习另一门语言有很多好处。

sentences.english: It opens doors, makes you more employable, helps you make new friends, and it’s fun too.
sentences.chinese: 它能为你打开机遇之门，让你更具就业竞争力，帮助你结交新朋友，而且学习过程本身也充满乐趣。

sentences.english: But to improve our linguistic skills, many of us have to endure hours of school lessons or evening classes, with our heads buried in textbooks.
sentences.chinese: 但为了提升语言技能，我们很多人不得不忍受很久的课堂教学或夜校课程，埋头于课本之中。

sentences.english: It’s no wonder then that technology appears to be providing a better and more accessible way of learning.
sentences.chinese: 因此，技术似乎能够提供一种更好、更便捷的学习方式，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.english: There is certainly a huge demand for language learning, and having a smartphone means you can have a virtual teacher with you wherever you go.
sentences.chinese: 语言学习的需求无疑非常巨大，而拥有智能手机意味着你无论走到哪里，都能拥有一位虚拟老师。

sentences.english: Many app developers are keen to cash in on the demand, and there are numerous learning apps available – including our own, free, BBC Learning English app!
sentences.chinese: 许多应用程序开发者都急于抓住这一需求商机，市面上涌现出了大量学习类应用——包括我们免费的BBC英语学习应用！

sentences.english: One of many popular apps, Duolingo, offers 91 courses in 30 languages and has more than 300 million users.
sentences.chinese: 多邻国（Duolingo）就是其中一款热门应用，它提供30种语言的91门课程，用户数量已超过3亿。

sentences.english: Some educational apps offer languages not popular enough to be taught at evening classes, or at most universities.
sentences.chinese: 一些教育类应用会提供那些不够热门、无法在夜校或大多数大学里学到的语言课程。

sentences.english: And others offer ‘invented’ language courses in Esperanto, Elvish and Star Trek's Klingon – lessons you might not find in a traditional classroom.
sentences.chinese: 还有一些应用提供世界语、精灵语、《星际迷航》中的克林贡语等“人造语言”课程——这些课程在传统课堂上你可能根本找不到。

sentences.english: Whatever you want to learn, apps allow you to go at your own pace and fit learning around other commitments.
sentences.chinese: 无论你想学什么，应用程序都能让你按照自己的节奏学习，并能在其他事务中灵活安排学习时间。

sentences.english: But they’re not perfect – you might not get your head round the grammar and will lack the peer support you could get in a classroom environment.
sentences.chinese: 但它们并非完美无缺——你可能无法理解语法知识，而且会缺少在课堂环境中能获得的同伴支持。

sentences.english: So, does technology spell the end of traditional classrooms and teachers?
sentences.chinese: 那么，技术是否意味着传统课堂和教师的终结呢？

sentences.english: Guy Baron, head of modern languages at Aberystwyth University, thinks not.
sentences.chinese: 阿伯里斯特威斯大学现代语言学院院长盖伊·巴伦并不这么认为。

sentences.english: He told the BBC that apps should be used alongside classroom methods, not to the exclusion of traditional teaching.
sentences.chinese: 他向英国广播公司表示，应用程序应与课堂教学方法结合使用，而不是排斥传统教学。

sentences.english: And he adds: "The apps are very conversational... they're not designed for degrees, but they could be additional resources."
sentences.chinese: 他还补充道：“这些应用程序非常注重对话交流……它们并非为学位课程设计，但可以作为额外的学习资源。”

sentences.english: Certainly technology is going to help in and outside the classroom.
sentences.chinese: 技术无疑会在课堂内外提供帮助。

sentences.english: But attending a real lesson, facing a real teacher, probably forces you to be more committed.
sentences.chinese: 但参加真实的课程，面对真实的老师，可能会迫使你更加投入。

sentences.english: Motivation can be a problem when using an app.
sentences.chinese: 使用应用程序学习时，动力可能是一个问题。

sentences.english: But if you have a genuine and practical reason to learn another language, you will no doubt stick with it.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你有真实和现实的理由去学习另一门语言，你无疑会坚持下去。
